claim: Intrinsic self-correction on reasoning tasks fails and can lower accuracy.
quote: their performance even degrades after self-correction
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Turn critique-only revision OFF; revise only on real check output.

claim: Earlier self-correction gains came from oracle labels or weak first prompts, and debate did not beat equal-count self-consistency (search-result summary of the paper, not the abstract page).
quote: multi-agent debate, when compared with an equivalent number of responses, does not outperform self-consistency
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Compare any multi-call design to plain self-consistency at equal calls.

claim: Self-correction works only with reliable external feedback; no prompted-LLM-only success was found.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
transfer: Gate revision on program-run feedback.

claim: Self-repair in code gives modest, uneven gains once repair cost is counted.
quote: performance gains are often modest, vary a lot between subsets of the data, and are sometimes not present at all
title: Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
transfer: Compare repair against fresh samples at equal tokens.

claim: Self-repair is limited by the model's feedback on its own code; stronger feedback gives larger gains.
quote: self-repair is bottlenecked by the model's ability to provide feedback on its own code
title: Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
transfer: Feedback must come from execution or a separate stronger signal.

claim: GPT-4 is no better at verifying solutions than generating them; critique content barely matters to iterative prompting gains.
quote: The correctness and content of the criticisms seems largely irrelevant to the performance of iterative prompting
title: GPT-4 Doesn't Know It's Wrong: An Analysis of Iterative Prompting for Reasoning Problems
n: graph coloring task (not seen on page)
transfer: Do not use a model judge as verifier; use a program.

claim: Multi-agent debate does not reliably beat other prompting strategies unless tuned.
quote: multi-agent debating systems, in their current form, do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies
title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
transfer: Skip debate; use forced divergence plus pruning on open tasks.

claim: Multi-agent LLM systems often give minimal gains on popular benchmarks.
quote: their performance gains on popular benchmarks are often minimal
title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
transfer: Keep one agent; adding roles needs an equal-token test.

claim: CoT gains concentrate on math and logic; on MMLU CoT matches direct answering unless an equals sign appears.
quote: on MMLU, CoT matches direct answering unless the question or response contains an equals sign
authors: Sprague, Yin, Rodriguez, Jiang, Wadhwa, Singhal, Zhao, Ye, Mahowald, Durrett
title: To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
n: 100+ papers, 20 datasets, 14 models (per earlier brief; abstract page showed 20 datasets, 14 models)
transfer: Format gate: CoT only for math or symbolic items.

claim: CoT can sharply lower accuracy on tasks where thinking hurts people; o1-preview lost up to 36.3 points versus GPT-4o.
quote: CoT costing OpenAI o1-preview up to 36.3% absolute accuracy compared to GPT-4o
authors: Liu, Geng, Wu, Sucholutsky, Lombrozo, Griffiths
title: Mind Your Step (by Step): Chain-of-Thought can Reduce Performance on Tasks where Thinking Makes Humans Worse
transfer: Route perception-like and exception-heavy items to direct answers.

claim: Explicit CoT degrades instruction-following accuracy and pulls attention off instruction tokens.
quote: explicit CoT reasoning can significantly degrade instruction-following accuracy
title: When Thinking Fails: The Pitfalls of Reasoning for Instruction-Following in LLMs
transfer: Skip CoT on constraint-following tasks, or check constraints in code.

claim: Longer reasoning lowered accuracy on distractor, spurious-feature and deduction tasks; Claude models grew more distracted.
quote: Claude models become increasingly distracted by irrelevant information
title: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
n: synthetic task families, several large reasoning models
transfer: Cap thinking length; test a cap per suite.

claim: o1-like models spend heavy compute on simple problems with little gain.
quote: excessive computational resources are allocated for simple problems with minimal benefit
title: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
transfer: Probe first with a short answer; escalate only on disagreement.

claim: Standard models beat reasoning models on simple tasks; both collapse at high complexity; effort falls while budget remains.
quote: their reasoning effort increases with problem complexity up to a point, then declines despite having remaining token budget
authors: Shojaee, Mirzadeh, Alizadeh, Horton, Bengio, Farajtabar
title: The Illusion of Thinking
venue: arXiv preprint (later critiques of its setup exist, not checked)
transfer: Keep a direct arm; do not assume more thinking helps on simple items.

claim: Adding one seemingly relevant clause cut accuracy by up to 65%; changing only numbers lowered all models' accuracy.
quote: Adding a single clause that seems relevant to the question causes significant performance drops (up to 65%)
authors: Mirzadeh, Alizadeh, Shahrokhi, Tuzel, Bengio, Farajtabar
title: GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
transfer: Test every method on perturbed variants, not only original items.

claim: CoT gains in planning appear only with problem-specific prompts and decay as problem size grows.
quote: those improvements quickly deteriorate as the size n of the query-specified stack grows
title: Chain of Thoughtlessness? An Analysis of CoT in Planning
transfer: Do not trust generic CoT prompts out of distribution.

claim: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the real reason for a prediction; biased models justify wrong answers.
quote: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the true reason for a model's prediction
title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
transfer: Do not use the written rationale as evidence of correctness.

claim: Reasoning models often reveal hints they used in under 20% of cases.
quote: the reveal rate is often below 20%
title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
transfer: Monitor outputs and code checks, not rationale text.

claim: LLM evaluators score their own outputs higher; self-recognition correlates linearly with the bias.
quote: a linear correlation between self-recognition capability and the strength of self-preference bias
title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
transfer: Use a non-model check or a different judge, never the same model self-grading.

claim: Without a verifier, majority voting and reward models plateau beyond several hundred samples; with one, coverage rose 15.9% to 56% over 250 samples.
quote: plateau beyond several hundred samples
authors: Brown, Juravsky, Ehrlich, Clark, Le, Re, Mirhoseini
title: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
transfer: Sampling pays only with a check; otherwise selection is the limit.

claim: Self-consistency gain was +17.9 on GSM8K but only +3.9 on ARC-challenge and +6.4 on StrategyQA, so gains shrink off arithmetic.
quote: GSM8K (+17.9%), SVAMP (+11.0%), AQuA (+12.2%), StrategyQA (+6.4%) and ARC-challenge (+3.9%)
authors: Wang, Wei, Schuurmans, Le, Chi, Narang, Chowdhery, Zhou
title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
transfer: Expect small gains on commonsense items. Confirms the earlier brief's 17-point figure for GSM8K.

claim: Tree of Thoughts' headline gain is on Game of 24 (4% to 74%), a task with cheap partial-state scoring; the abstract reports no equal-compute control.
quote: GPT-4 with chain-of-thought prompting only solved 4% of tasks, our method achieved a success rate of 74%
authors: Yao, Yu, Zhao, Shafran, Griffiths, Cao, Narasimhan
title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
n: Game of 24 and 2 other tasks (from memory)
transfer: Use search only where partial states can be scored by code.

claim: Reflexion's 91% HumanEval is against GPT-4 at 80%; the abstract does not say which feedback type drove which task.
quote: Reflexion achieves a 91% pass@1 accuracy on the HumanEval coding benchmark
authors: Shinn, Cassano, Berman, Gopinath, Narasimhan, Yao
title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
transfer: Keep reflection check-gated; the gain depends on test feedback.

claim: Compute-optimal allocation gives over 4x efficiency versus best-of-N; beating a 14x larger model holds only where the small model already has non-trivial success.
quote: test-time compute can be used to outperform a 14x larger model
title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
transfer: Allocate by estimated difficulty; the gain needs a trained verifier.

claim: Small models do not consistently benefit from long CoT and do better with shorter, simpler chains (fine-tuning setting).
quote: they perform better when fine-tuned on shorter, simpler reasoning chains
title: Small Models Struggle to Learn from Strong Reasoners
transfer: Prefer short chains for small models; fine-tuning evidence only.
